bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Govt transfers Rs 1233cr as part of social security pension - The Pioneer
bihar_raw_news.content: September 11, 2026 Bihar Govt transfers Rs 1,233cr as part of social security pension Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Pioneer News Service Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Thursday transferred over Rs 1,233 crore directly to the bank accounts of 1.05 crore social security pensioners in the state. Each beneficiary, including senior citizens, widows and persons with disabilities, gets Rs 1,100 through direct benefit transfer, officials said. “The CM transferred Rs 1,233.87 crore through DBT to the bank accounts of 1.05 crore social security pensioners at a function in Munger,” an official said. As many as 98,896 new beneficiaries were added to the scheme, he said. While speaking on the occasion, the CM said social security pension would be transferred directly to beneficiaries’ bank accounts through DBT on the 10th of every month. Choudhary said the government was committed to ensuring that eligible people receive social security benefits without discrimination and that welfare schemes reach beneficiaries directly. The CM also laid the foundation stone for the widening and strengthening of a stretch of National Highway 333 from Gangta in Munger to Kodwarva in Jamui. 0 Likes 0 Dislikes Bookmark 0 Comments Leave a Comment

bihar_raw_news.title: High-level review meeting regarding preparations for 'Seva Sankalp Abhiyan' concludes ...
bihar_raw_news.content: High-level review meeting regarding preparations for 'Seva Sankalp Abhiyan' concludes under chairmanship of Chief Secretary of Bihar ANI | Updated: Sep 11, 2026 17:01 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Patna ( Bihar ) [India], September 11 (ANI): A high-level review meeting was held under the chairmanship of Bihar Chief Secretary Pratyaya Amrit to discuss the comprehensive preparations and successful implementation of the 'Seva Sankalp Abhiyan' (Service Pledge Campaign), scheduled to take place from September 17 to October 17. According to a press release, Principal Secretaries and Secretaries from various state departments attended the meeting in person, while District Magistrates from all districts joined via video conferencing. During the review, the Chief Secretary assessed the department-wise status of all 13 key components of the campaign and directed officials to complete preparations in a time-bound manner. The release noted that the campaign will commence on the evening of September 17 with the 'Aashirwad ka Diya' (Lamp of Blessing) program, involving the collective lighting of lamps in every household across the state and at a minimum of 10 prominent or symbolic public locations in each district. To facilitate this, lamps will be distributed to beneficiaries through Jeevika, urban local bodies, and the Public Distribution System. Additionally, between September 17 and October 7, painting and speech competitions based on the theme 'Viksit Bharat Sankalp' (Developed India Pledge) will be organised in all government and private schools under the 'Seva Chitra' initiative, alongside Parent-Teacher Meetings (PTMs). To raise public awareness, 18-20 theatre troupes will be formed under the 'Seva Smaran' (Service Remembrance) initiative; these troupes will perform street plays in schools, colleges, and panchayats, with special performances scheduled for October 2, the release said. Furthermore, a three-day event titled 'Aangan ka Milan' (Gathering in the Courtyard) will be held at all Anganwadi centres from September 25 to October 7. This event will feature the honouring of Anganwadi and ASHA workers, interactions with beneficiary mothers, and recreational activities for children, alongside the dissemination of information regarding nutrition and health schemes, the release added. To highlight the positive changes brought about in people's lives by government schemes, district and state-level digital data banks will be created by compiling authentic reels and short videos under the 'Kahani Badlav Ki' (Story of Change) component. Additionally, 'Seva Jyoti Yatra' will feature foot marches, as well as bicycle and motorcycle rallies across the state and districts; volunteers from 'Mera Yuva Bharat' will participate in these events, culminating in a collective pledge for 'Viksit Bharat 2047' (Developed India 2047). As the nationwide 'Vadnagar to Varanasi (Jal, Jan, aur Seva Sankalp Yatra)' passes through Bihar , arrangements will be made for grand receptions, security, accommodation, and interactions with local beneficiaries at designated stopover points, the release noted. To foster public participation, 25 activities, including the cleaning of ponds and Chhath ghats, tree plantation, and sanitation drives, will be conducted under the 'Seva Mera Yogdan' (Service: My Contribution) initiative, ensuring visible, on-ground transformation at a minimum of two locations in every assembly

bihar_raw_news.title: Rethinking Policy for India's Divergent Demographic Dividend Across States
bihar_raw_news.content: Views are personal. The sixth National Family Health Survey puts India's total fertility rate at 2.0 children per woman, below the replacement level of 2.1 for a second consecutive round. Thirty-four of India's thirty-six states and union territories are now at or below replacement fertility. Only Bihar and Meghalaya remain above it. Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand and Manipur, three of the five states above replacement in 2019–21, have converged at 2.1. Rural India has reached replacement fertility for the first time, after urban India did in 2005–06. The population-explosion narrative that shaped India for decades is giving way to a broad-based fertility transition. But fertility is converging faster than age structures. India's demographic dividend is therefore no longer a national asset with one national deadline. It is a set of state-level windows: some still widening, some near their peak and others already closing. Yet skills, fiscal and industrial policy continue to be designed largely around the national average. What the Demographic Dividend Can Deliver A demographic window opens when the working-age population grows relative to dependents; whether it produces a dividend depends on whether those workers are productively employed. For India, the demographic contribution to per-capita income growth is estimated to peak around 2031 at roughly 2.1 percentage points. By 2041 that contribution halves; by 2061 it is gone. The tailwind is real, but modest relative to the growth India needs. The Viksit Bharat objective of $18,000 per capita by 2047 requires per-capita income growth above 7 percent a year for more than two decades. The rest must come from productivity and participation. India's low female labour force participation makes women's employment one particularly large unused margin, although raising it would also increase the number of people seeking productive work. One Country, Three Demographic Clocks India increasingly contains three demographic economies: younger states such as Uttar Pradesh and Bihar where the working-age population is still expanding; states such as Maharashtra around their workforce peak; and much of the South, where workforce growth has flattened or reversed and ageing is accelerating. Central India's working-age share will continue rising until 2051; every other region has peaked. The Southern region's working-age share falls from 67 to 58 percent, while its over-60 population more than doubles to 29 percent. Nationally, the median age rises from 29 to 40 by 2051 and the share aged 65 and over from 7 to 17 percent. By then, India's age profile will resemble that of China and the United States today. The divergence is sharper across states. Uttar Pradesh's working-age population climbs to 132 million by 2051 and Bihar's to 111 million, while Maharashtra peaks and slips and Tamil Nadu flattens. Uttar Pradesh accounts for an amount equivalent to 78 percent of India's net working-age gain and Bihar another 52 percent; their shares exceed 100 percent because working-age populations decline elsewhere, including Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu and West Bengal. This creates a large but temporary employment requirement. India needs an estimated six million jobs annually to absorb the expected increase

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar to set up 25 new sugar mills under Sugarcane Investment Policy 2026 - ChiniMandi
bihar_raw_news.content: All News English Indian Sugar News Sugar News Top News Trendings Patna: The Bihar government is targeting the establishment of 25 new sugar mills and other sugarcane-based industries as part of its efforts to attract investment and expand the state’s sugarcane economy, Patna Press reported. The key features of the Bihar Sugarcane Investment Policy 2026 were presented to domestic and international investors at a two-day conference held in New Delhi on September 9 and 10. Sugarcane Minister Sanjay Kumar said the state has identified the establishment of 25 new sugar mills as a key investment target, along with industries based on sugarcane and its by-products. The government is seeking to move beyond conventional sugar production by promoting value-added industries linked to the sugarcane sector. The policy is expected to create opportunities for investment across sugar processing and downstream industries. The state has also assured prospective investors of support in securing land and obtaining necessary approvals. Bihar official Vedvrat Kumar highlighted the advantages of establishing industrial projects in the state and said the government would facilitate investors during the initial stages of project development. Ethanol and bio-energy projects are among the key areas being promoted under the investment push. The government is encouraging investments in ethanol production, power generation and bio-energy based on sugarcane and its by-products. Officials said such projects could help generate additional employment and income opportunities while increasing the value derived from sugarcane. The government is also promoting initiatives involving fertilisers, seeds and modern agricultural machinery to support sugarcane cultivation and improve opportunities for farmers. A dedicated Bihar government stall at the New Delhi conference showcased the Sugarcane Investment Policy 2026 and investment opportunities available in the state. According to the department, several business representatives expressed interest in setting up industrial units in Bihar. The conference brought together experts and representatives from major Indian and international companies, who discussed developments in the sugar market and modern sugarcane cultivation techniques. The event was organised with the support of the Government of India and the Sugar Association and was inaugurated by Union Secretary Santosh Kumar Sarangi. With a target of 25 new sugar mills and a wider focus on ethanol, power and bio-energy, Bihar is seeking to position sugarcane as a driver of broader industrial development and attract private investment into the sector.

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Plans 500 MW Rooftop Solar For Govt Buildings Under RESCO Model - Saur Energy
bihar_raw_news.content: News Solar Bihar Plans 500 MW Rooftop Solar For Govt Buildings Under RESCO Model The RESCO structure is expected to enable solar deployment on government buildings without requiring the building owner to undertake the complete project development. Manish Kumar 11 Sep 2026 09:41 IST Follow Us Bihar Plans 500 MW Rooftop Solar For Govt Buildings Under RESCO Model Photograph: (AI) The Bihar Renewable Energy Development Agency (BREDA) has initiated a tender process to empanel solar power developers for setting up 500 MW of grid-connected rooftop solar projects on government buildings across the state under the Renewable Energy Service Company (RESCO) model. Advertisment Under the tender, selected Solar Power Developers (SPDs) will be responsible for the design, engineering, supply, installation, testing, commissioning, operation and maintenance of the rooftop solar plants, according to a tender extension notice issued by BREDA. The tender has been floated now which seeks empanelment of SPDs for the 500 MW programme. Advertisment No Proposed Tariff The RESCO structure is expected to enable solar deployment on government buildings without requiring the government building owner to undertake the complete upfront project development and operational responsibilities. However, the tender extension notice does not specify the proposed tariff, project-wise capacity allocation, contract tenure, financing structure or payment mechanism. BREDA has revised the tender schedule, with online sale of the tender document beginning from September 10, 2026. The pre-bid meeting is scheduled for September 18 at 2:30 pm at BREDA's office in Patna. Advertisment Submission Dates Interested bidders can submit their tender documents online until 2 pm on October 5, 2026. Physical submission of the original EMD, tender document cost, bid processing fee and the required undertaking relating to non-blacklisting or debarment will be accepted until 2:30 pm on the same day. The techno-commercial bids are scheduled to be opened from 3:30 pm on October 5, while the date for opening of financial bids will be communicated separately to eligible bidders through email. Advertisment The proposed 500 MW programme could create a sizeable distributed solar pipeline across Bihar's government-building estate, while shifting project development, installation and long-term O&M responsibilities to empanelled private developers through the RESCO route. Advertisment However, details on the number and type of government buildings to be covered, individual rooftop capacities, expected generation, tariff discovery and the duration of the RESCO agreements are not provided in the tender extension notice and would need to be examined in the detailed RFP documents. Similar Tales From Other States Bihar's 500 MW programme comes amid a wider expansion of RESCO-based rooftop solar procurement for government buildings. In Uttar Pradesh, UPNEDA issued a tender in April 2025 for 500 MW of grid-connected rooftop solar PV projects on government and semi-government buildings and other institutions, with projects to be implemented under the RESCO model through tariff-based competitive bidding. The UP programme allowed capacities ranging from 1 kWp to 2 MWp and provided for net-metering or net-billing arrangements. Delhi has also pursued the model through IPGCL, which floated a 50 MW government-building rooftop solar programme

bihar_raw_news.title: IAS Ashish Modi OBC Certificate Controversy | Centre Seeks Jharkhand Report
bihar_raw_news.content: English News Local Rajasthan IAS Ashish Modi OBC Certificate Controversy | Centre Seeks Jharkhand Report Exclusive Questions raised over IAS Ashish Modi’s OBC certificate: Centre seeks report after 12 years; IAS claims Modi is OBC in Jharkhand Jaipur 15 hours ago Copy link Rajasthan-cadre IAS officer Ashish Modi’s OBC certificate has come under question 12 years after he joined the civil services. Ashish Modi is a 2014-batch IAS officer and secured the 350th rank under the OBC category. The issue has now gained attention over how an IAS officer belonging to the Vaishya community obtained an OBC certificate. On August 30, the Centre wrote to the Jharkhand Chief Secretary seeking a factual report on the entire matter. Ashish Modi has also been involved in controversies over his cadre change and a dispute with his wife. Centre seeks factual report On August 30, the Centre wrote to the Jharkhand government seeking a factual report on the matter. The report will examine the caste mentioned in the certificate submitted at the time of selection and the actual position according to the relevant government records. If the certificate is found to be invalid under the rules, his job could face trouble. Ashish Modi says Vaishya community is included in OBC list in Jharkhand IAS officer Ashish Modi said that the Vaishya community is included in the OBC category in Jharkhand. “I have not committed any fraud. My OBC certificate is valid. The caste mentioned in the certificate submitted at the time of selection and the relevant government records have been provided,” he said. The OBC list in Jharkhand mentions the ‘Modi’ caste. Modi’s family had moved to Giridih district years ago from Fatehpur in Rajasthan’s Sikar district. However, the final position will become clear only after verification of the original documents and the government investigation. Expert view: Job unlikely to face any problem To understand the technical aspects of the matter, Bhaskar spoke to Hari Kumar Godara, former secretary of the Rajasthan OBC Commission and a retired judge. He said that, to the best of his knowledge, the Vaishya community is included in the OBC category in the Central List for Bihar and Jharkhand. Therefore, Modi’s job is unlikely to face any problem. In Jharkhand, the surname Modi is included in the OBC category He said every state has a separate OBC list. A problem would arise if the Central List of OBC communities differs from the state list. The Vaishya community is included in the OBC list in Bihar. When Jharkhand was carved out of Bihar, the same provisions continued. This means the Vaishya community remained included in the OBC category in the state list. Former Congress national president Sitaram Kesri and former Bihar Deputy Chief Minister Sushil Modi belonged to the Vaishya community. Both were included in the OBC category. The Modi surname is also included in the OBC category in Gujarat. Chief Secretary says Centre has not sought information from him On the OBC controversy, Chief Secretary V. Srinivas said,

national_raw_news.content: The 18th BRICS Summit will begin at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi tomorrow, with the national capital putting its finishing touches in place for the grand event. The two day Summit will bring together eleven major emerging and developing economies, including Brazil, China, Egypt, Ethiopia, Indonesia, India, Iran, Russia, Saudi Arabia, South Africa, and the UAE. The theme of India’s Chairship 2026 is “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability.” World leaders including Russian President Vladimir Putin, Chinese President Xi Jinping, President of South Africa Cyril Ramaphosa, Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto, Iran President Masoud Pezeshkian, Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed al Nahyan and Prime Minister of Ethiopia Abiy Ahmed Ali will participate in the Summit. Brazil will be represented by Foreign Affairs Minister Mauro Vieira. Saudi Arabia’s Minister of Foreign Affairs, Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud will also participate in the Summit. Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, and Vietnamese Prime Minister Le Minh Hung are the other Heads of State who will attend the Summit. United Nations Secretary General António Guterres, Director-General of WHO, Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, and President of New Development Bank, Dilma Rousseff are among the Heads of International Organisations who will participate in the event. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is likely to hold bilateral talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin today. The President of Russia and Foreign Minister of Brazil arrived in the national capital last night to participate in the Summit. The President of South Africa is set to arrive this morning. Presidents of Iran, Indonesia, Egypt, Philippines, and Burundi, Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi, and Prime Ministers of Malaysia and Ethiopia, are scheduled to arrive later today. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will have a series of bilateral meetings on the sidelines of the Summit. Akashvani correspondent reports that the grouping was formalised during the BRIC Foreign Ministers’ Meeting, held on the margins of the United Nations General Assembly in New York in September 2006. The First BRIC Summit was held in Yekaterinburg, Russia, on 16th June 2009. BRIC expanded into BRICS with the inclusion of South Africa following the BRIC Foreign Ministers’ Meeting held in New York in September 2010. South Africa participated first time in the Third BRICS Summit, held in Sanya, China, in April 2011. BRICS further expanded in January 2024, when Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia and the UAE became full members of the grouping. India assumed the BRICS Chairship on 1st January this year. This marks India’s fourth Chairship of BRICS. India had earlier chaired BRICS in 2012, 2016 and 2021.

national_raw_news.content: In Cricket, India produced a brilliant all-round performance to thrash Bangladesh by 40 runs in the first semi-final of the Women’s Asia Cup 2026 in Dubai last night. India’s victory secured their place in the Women’s Asia Cup 2026 final, with the second semi-final between Sri Lanka and Pakistan determining their opponents. Chasing a target of 150 runs, Bangladesh struggled to build momentum as India’s bowlers kept the pressure on and made 109 for the loss of seven wickets in the stipulated twenty overs. Shorna Akter, unbeaten 22, was the top scorer for Bangladesh. For India, Deepti Sharma scalped three wickets, Nandani Sharma took two wickets, while Shree Charani and Prema Rawat claimed a wicket each. Earlier, Bangladesh won the toss and opted to field. Put in to bat, India posted 149/6 in 20 overs, with opener Shafali Verma anchoring the innings with a fluent 64 off 40 balls. She was declared Player of the Match. The victory sets up a mouth-watering final for Team India. In the second semi-final today, Pakistan will face Sri Lanka in Dubai. The match will start at 8 PM Indian Standard Time. The winner of that contest will meet India in the final on Sunday. With strong all-round contributions and a dominant bowling display, India have underlined their credentials as favourites to lift the Women’s Asia Cup 2026 title.

national_raw_news.title: Health Ministry's Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission holds national conference in ... - ANI News
national_raw_news.content: Health Ministry's Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission holds national conference in Bengaluru to strengthen safety and standards of biosimilar medicines Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर Health Ministry's Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission holds national conference in Bengaluru to strengthen safety and standards of biosimilar medicines ANI | Updated: Sep 11, 2026 18:19 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], September 11 (ANI): The Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission (IPC), an autonomous institution under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, organised a two-day National Conference on “Quality and Safety of Biosimilars : Strengthening India’s Biopharma SHAKTI Vision” on September 10–11, 2026, at the Centre for Cellular and Molecular Platforms (C-CAMP), Bengaluru. According to a press release issued by the Health Ministry, the conference was attended by 160 participants from regulatory authorities, industry, academia, research organisations, and other stakeholder groups. The conference was organised by IPC in collaboration with the Indian Drug Manufacturers’ Association (IDMA), with the Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council (BIRAC) and Centre for Cellular and Molecular Platforms (C-CAMP) serving as Knowledge Partners, and the Karnataka Drugs and Pharmaceuticals Manufacturers’ Association (KDPMA) as the Associate Partner. The conference aligns with the Government of India’s Biopharma SHAKTI Vision to strengthen India’s biopharmaceutical ecosystem through innovation, self-reliance, quality and global competitiveness. The conference addressed key scientific and regulatory challenges associated with the development, evaluation and safety of biosimilars, with emphasis on pharmacopoeial standards, critical quality attributes, analytical characterisation, comparability assessment, immunogenicity, pharmacovigilance and evolving regulatory expectations. A major highlight of the conference was the release of the Indian Pharmacopoeia Reference Substance (IPRS) for Enoxaparin Sodium for bioassays. Enoxaparin Sodium is a low-molecular-weight heparin and anticoagulant widely used for the prevention and treatment of thromboembolic disorders. The IPRS for Enoxaparin Sodium for bioassays may serve as an authenticated reference material for bioassay testing, supporting accurate, consistent, and comparable assessment of its biological activity. The release of the IPRS marks an important advancement in strengthening the availability of authenticated pharmacopoeial reference substances for bioassay-related testing of Enoxaparin Sodium, while contributing to the Atmanirbhar Bharat vision by strengthening India’s indigenous pharmaceutical quality infrastructure. As per the release, the inaugural session was addressed by distinguished representatives from IPC, SLA-Karnataka, NIB, IDMA, C-CAMP, and BIRAC, who emphasised the importance of strengthening quality, safety, and regulatory confidence in biosimilars. The session also highlighted the need for sustained collaboration among regulatory authorities, pharmacopoeial institutions, industry, academia, and research organisations to support the development of a robust and globally competitive biopharmaceutical sector. Addressing the participants, V Kalaiselvan, Secretary-cum-Scientific Director, IPC, highlighted the importance of strengthening pharmacopoeial standards, reliable analytical evaluation, safety monitoring, and regulatory cooperation to ensure the quality and safety of biosimilars. He also emphasised the need to align Indian practices with evolving regulatory expectations, support biopharmaceutical innovation, and contribute to the vision of Viksit Bharat. Technical sessions featured experts from IPC, SLA, WHO, USP, NIB, IDMA, BIRAC, C-CAMP, and leading biopharmaceutical organisations, providing perspectives spanning pharmacopoeial standard-setting, regulatory science, analytical development, safety monitoring, and innovation in biologics. national_raw_news.content: PIB Lucknow, UP Information Department Host Media Dialogue With Kerala Journalists To Boost Cultural Exchange Home Uttar-pradesh PIB Lucknow, UP Information Department Host Media Dialogue With Kerala Journalists To Boost Cultural Exchange PIB Lucknow, UP Information Department Host Media Dialogue With Kerala Journalists To Boost Cultural Exchange PIB Lucknow and the Uttar Pradesh Information and Public Relations Department organised a ‘Media Samvaad’ programme with Kerala journalists in Lucknow. The interaction focused on cultural exchange, governance models, media practices and development experiences. Journalists discussed UP’s law and order system, Kerala’s education performance and the role of cinema in cultural integration. Agencies Updated: Friday, September 11, 2026, 05:50 PM IST PIB Lucknow, UP Information Department Host Media Dialogue With Kerala Journalists To Boost Cultural Exchange | X - dayalg343 Lucknow, September 11: A ‘Media Samvaad’ program was organized jointly by the Press Information Bureau, Lucknow (PIB) and the Uttar Pradesh Information and Public Relations Department under the joint aegis of both departments. The program was organized with media representatives from Keralam. The program aimed to promote mutual dialogue and exchange of experiences, understand each other’s culture and development journey, and gain insights into media functioning. It also aimed to strengthen the spirit of ‘Ek Bharat-Shreshtha Bharat’ and promote mutual understanding and cooperation. A delegation of media representatives from leading electronic and print media organizations of Keralam, led by the Press Information Bureau, Lucknow, visited Lucknow. During the visit, journalists from Keralam gained an understanding of the culture, development and governance model of Uttar Pradesh. They particularly showed interest in Uttar Pradesh’s law and order model. They learned about the concrete efforts to strengthen law and order in the state, as well as the government’s dialogue with the public and mechanisms for receiving feedback. The journalists from Uttar Pradesh expressed interest in the education system of Keralam and the reasons behind its better performance. Representatives from both sides also shared their experiences regarding media functioning and coverage of local and public-interest issues. During the program, they also discussed the relationship between Bollywood and the South Indian film industry, and the role of cinema in promoting cultural exchange across the country. The program was held under the direction of Director, Information, Vishal Singh, and Director, PIB Lucknow, Dileep Kumar Shukla. Director, PIB Keralam Ms V. national_raw_news.title: Pune Airport's Renovated Old Terminal Nears Reopening, Awaits Final BCAS Clearance
national_raw_news.content: Pune Airport's Renovated Old Terminal Nears Reopening, Awaits Final BCAS Clearance News Brief Pune Airport's Renovated Old Terminal Nears Reopening, Awaits Final BCAS Clearance Arun Dhital Sep 11, 2026 | Updated 10:48 AM GMT+5:30 Save & read from anywhere! Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app . Sign In Prefer Prefer The upcoming terminal building of Pune Airport (PIB) Pune airport's renovated old terminal is close to reopening, with only a security clearance pending. Union minister of state for civil aviation Murlidhar Mohol inspected the upgraded check-in and security-hold areas on Thursday (10 September). Mohol said, "The number of passengers at Pune airport is steadily increasing. Therefore, our priority is not only to provide better facilities but also to reduce congestion during peak hours. The renovation of the old terminal building and its more effective utilisation has been completed. Most of the required procedures are over, and only the final BCAS approval remains. Instructions have also been issued to BCAS, and the old terminal will soon be available to Pune passengers in a modern and upgraded form". The 4,075 square metre facility holds check-in, pre-embarkation security check and security hold areas, with 14 CUTE-enabled counters, three XBIS machines at check-in, four XBIS units and eight door frame metal detectors in the security check zone, and two boarding gates numbered 6A and 6B. It also sets aside 66.40 square metres for retail and 70.13 square metres for food outlets, adds a baby-care room and more seats with power sockets, and will run Digi Yatra once BCAS approves. Airport director Santosh Dhoke said, "A team from Mumbai-based 'Vikas' recently inspected the old terminal. After the inspection, they did not point out any deficiencies. A team from Delhi will now conduct the final inspection. If the team does not issue any further instructions, the terminal will be opened to passengers soon." Hourly capacity should rise by about 405 passengers at an airport handling nearly 34,000 travellers daily. Fire clearance came in May and the readiness exercise was completed in July. Frequent flyer Kritika Mihalani said the renovated terminal distributing passenger load better "will make travelling much more convenient". national_raw_news.content: Union Minister Rijiju distributes shields, prizes to winners of National Youth Parliament Competition 2025-26 Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर Union Minister Rijiju distributes shields, prizes to winners of National Youth Parliament Competition 2025-26 ANI | Updated: Sep 10, 2026 21:15 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], September 10 (ANI): Union Minister for Parliamentary Affairs and Minority Affairs Kiren Rijiju on Thursday felicitated the winners of the 27th National Youth Parliament Competition 2025-26 for Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas, with PM Shri Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya, Ukhrul-1, Manipur, securing the top position at the national level. Rijiju distributed shields, trophies and prizes to the winning teams at a prize distribution ceremony held at the GMC Balayogi Auditorium, Parliament Library Building, Parliament House Complex, New Delhi. Congratulating the national winner and seven regional winners, Rijiju underlined the importance of Parliament as a cornerstone of democracy and urged students to understand the functioning of parliamentary institutions. Addressing the gathering, the Union Minister said parliamentary democracy is best suited to India, where citizens exercise their democratic rights through elected representatives. He also appreciated the contribution of Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas in nurturing students and shaping their character. Secretary, Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs, Nikunja Bihari Dhal, congratulated the winning teams and highlighted the role of Youth Parliament programmes in developing students' personalities, critical-thinking abilities and spirit of teamwork. Additional Secretary, Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs, Dr Satya Prakash, emphasised the contribution of principals, teachers and students in nation-building. Referring to the traditional Guru-Shishya Parampara, he said their collective efforts are important for realising the vision of a developed India by 2047. The students of PM Shri Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya, Ukhrul-1, Manipur, also presented a repeat performance of their Youth Parliament during the ceremony. The Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs has been organising Youth Parliament competitions for Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas for nearly 30 years. The 27th edition was conducted during 2025-26 among 100 Vidyalayas across eight regions of the Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti. The programme aims to familiarise students with parliamentary practices and procedures, while encouraging discussion, debate, self-confidence, leadership qualities, critical thinking and effective oratory. The Pt. Jawahar Lal Nehru Running Parliamentary Shield and national-level trophy were awarded to PM Shri Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya, Ukhrul-1, Manipur, representing the Shillong Region. The seven regional winners included PM Shri Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya, Kollam, Kerala (Hyderabad Region); PM Shri Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya, Theog, Shimla (Chandigarh Region); PM Shri Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya, Suratgarh, Sriganganagar (Jaipur Region); PM Shri Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya, Bilaspur, Chhattisgarh (Bhopal Region); PM Shri Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya, Valsad, Gujarat (Pune Region); PM Shri Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya, Purulia, West Bengal (Patna Region); and PM Shri Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya, Udham Singh Nagar, Uttarakhand (Lucknow Region). Deputy Secretary, Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs, Anil Kumar, delivered the vote of thanks and expressed gratitude to the distinguished guests, participating students, teachers, ministry officials and other stakeholders for their contribution to the successful conduct of the competition. national_raw_news.title: Meghalaya expands rubber cultivation thanks to Kerala institute
national_raw_news.content: Meghalaya expands rubber cultivation thanks to Kerala institute - Meghalaya Monitor Share Facebook X LinkedIn Pinterest Reddit Skype Messenger Messenger WhatsApp Telegram Viber Share via Email Print Kottayam, Sept 10 : The Rubber Research Institute of India (RRII), Kerala is giving focus to Meghalaya to expand rubber cultivation. A media delegation from Meghalaya and Sikkim, on a press tour to Kerala organised by the Press Information Bureau (PIB), visited the Rubber Research Institute of India and learnt about rubber cultivation, research, processing and value addition, with particular reference to the growth of the sector in Meghalaya. M. Vasanthgesan, Executive Director, RRII, led the interaction. Dr. Debabrata Rai, Director (Research), Dr. Siju T, Rubber Production Commissioner; and Priya Varma, Director (Training) were also present. The Executive Director highlighted the significant expansion of rubber cultivation in Meghalaya, where the area under rubber has increased from around 10,000 hectares more than a decade ago to approximately 33,000 hectares at present. The growth reflects increasing interest among farmers in rubber as a plantation crop with long-term income potential. Advertisement The delegation was briefed on the Rubber Board’s support to growers in Meghalaya through its Regional Office at Tura and eight field stations across the state, particularly in the Garo Hills. The field network provides technical assistance for plantation development and management. Rubber cultivation has an important socioeconomic dimension for farming communities, as mature trees can provide regular latex yields for several decades. The long-term income potential makes the crop an important plantation-based livelihood for growers in the state. The interaction also covered the role of Rubber Producers’ Societies (RPS) in enabling growers to collectively access technical assistance, infrastructure and processing facilities. There are approximately 2,600 RPSs across India, including more than 300 in the Northeast. In Meghalaya, efforts have also focused on improving the management of existing plantations. Around 2,000–3,000 hectares of rubber plantations were already present in the state, but some were not being tapped or managed systematically, affecting productivity. The intervention has supported their revival and improved management. Two Group Processing Centres (GPCs) were established last year under Green Hill RPS and Laurel Hills RPS in the Mendipathar area. The centres enable growers to collectively process latex into rubber sheets, allowing value addition closer to the point of production and potentially improving farm-gate returns compared with the sale of raw latex. The delegation was also informed about the dealer network for rubber across the Northeast, including Meghalaya, which provides established marketing channels for growers. While Sikkim does not have significant rubber cultivation, the visit provided its media representatives an opportunity to understand the wider rubber value chain and the scope for downstream processing and value-added activities associated with the sector. The delegation also learnt about the role of the Rubber Research Station in Meghalaya, which undertakes research and provides technical guidance suited to the state’s agro-climatic conditions.
